notes.title: Development Diary #1 - Finding the sound of bureaucratic machinery
notes.content:
“[i]We need to get rid of that placeholder 80s funk music, and we have full confidence in you,[/i]”  they told me once when I was joining the promising student (back then) team Outside the Fox. I am Jan Knot, the [strike]music composer and sound designer[/strike] Minister of Noise, and you are reading a [b]development diary about the music of Silicomrades[/b]. Yes, you will find out how big of an orchestra we require to perform the soundtrack live, but first, we need to return all the way back to the beginning of the iterative process, because we are ready to admit all the blind alleys that we encountered along the way.

[h1]Looking for the right musical style of Lawtvia[/h1]

If you've seen the trailer, played the demo, or taken part in Ministry of Testing, you already know what the final music sounds like in the game. But there [b]were many iterations[/b] before we arrived there. First drafts were heavily based on various industrial, orchestral, and ethno percussions and drums. We tried to convey an impression that all robots in Lawtvia are just simple instruments in our very totalitarian and utilitarian world. 

For the first listen, it was interesting, but sadly got boring very quickly. Around the time we also started messing with the adaptive music for the first time, with the clear goal of having all the music transitions in-game made smoothly based on the current state of the mission. For prototyping, I prepared various placeholder drum tracks for needed states (calm, action, etc), and they stayed in some places of the game for muuuuch longer than we would like to admit. I really don't want to write the exact number of years, I mean, I don’t even remember anymore. But the ominous “dum du du dummm” has certainly etched into our skulls in almost a hypnotic way, similar to a welded nut and bolt. Go on, give it a listen.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eEnSOVKL6uc

Anyway, after that phase, I experimented in a different direction, and tried my luck with fully analogue synth music, in order to evoke a feeling of a grim futuristic world. Some interesting ideas and melodies were created, but overall, it didn’t quite fit right with the visuals and direction Silicomrades were heading in. However, there was one [b]specific word[/b] that I wrote that still lingered on my mind, ready to make an important comeback later on. [b]Industrial[/b]!

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K16skcB8Hn0

It was back then that I suddenly realized that our robots are made from metal, and the whole robotic world is built on metal (okay, maybe also tons of concrete); therefore, our game should sound [b]metallic[/b]. Sounds obvious in retrospect, but it was a huge moment when I realized that I had to make metal music. And with that, I of course mean [b]heavy usage of brass instruments[/b]. 

First, I started experimenting with a combination of them and an analogue synth, which led to quite unique pieces. However, it again didn’t somehow fit into the game, at least not as much as I wanted to. So I went [b]full metal symphonist[/b], full heavy brass staccatos and chords, accompanied by big percussion, and among them was an anvil. Yes, “industrial” was truly the key. The whole team agreed wholeheartedly that [b]THIS[/b] is the direction we’ll be going for. Exactly the kind of music that a robo-bureaucrat would listen to to increase his efficiency, and imperial (and kafkaesque) march.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bHb9xIM9Bqk

[h1]Adaptive music system - Being smooth and unpredictable[/h1]

Now was finally the time to begin designing the system itself. That’s one of the greatest unique quirks of making videogame music - it has to be dynamic somehow, to not become repetitive and thus annoying. We put together plans for when and how the music should change at every one of the [b]11 missions[/b] of the game. Sometimes it’s a simple change based on players’ location, sometimes it is triggered by the number of enemies on screen, or by your time running out. And sometimes, it’s a combination. Take a look inside the [b]FMOD Studio[/b] where we prepared our adaptive music, and when you will be playing Silicomrades in the future, try to concentrate on the music and try to guess when and why the music has changed. There is truly rhyme and reason behind everything!

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Fz1YosVRtOY

[h1]First finalized music pieces, fresh out of the assembly line[/h1]

Now the puzzle pieces were coming along - I already knew the general musical style, when it would play in-game, and how it would behave. So nothing was stopping me from going all-in and starting to (finally) compose the pieces you now hear in the game. I created several themes for our [b]rebellious low-quality robots[/b], some of which you can, for example, hear in the main menu screens. I also applied a slightly different musical style for each episode, to underline the differences in environment, mood, and game mechanics ([b]there is a new one in every mission![/b]).  

Most notable is our forest [b]Campfire Carnage[/b] episode, where I used guitars and contrabass to kind of mimic [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czech_tramping_music]tramp[/url] (country) music style. I composed it in small segments that would switch, loop, and transition whenever needed, and thus created quite an adaptive musical score.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lai6pgTzaoM

[h1]Instruments and mixing - One man virtual orchestra[/h1]

First, I have to clarify that all instruments you hear are virtual (digital) and were recorded by various professionals at different places.  I am using those sounds in my sound-cave all alone with my PC. Would I want it to be recorded live? Of course! Even if it's just a small piece. Maybe one day. But there is an important question - How many musicians would I need? And which instruments are used?

[b]Brass section:[/b] 2 tubas, cimbasso, contrabass trombone, 2 bass trombones, 4 tenor trombones, 2 euphoniums, 6 horns, and 3 trumpets. [b]Woodwind section:[/b] piccolo, flute, bass flute, 2 clarinets, bass clarinet and contrabass clarinet. [b]String section:[/b] 3 guitars and 1 contrabass. What’s the count at the moment? Well, we still have [b]percussion[/b] left: 3 snare drums, 4 tom sets, 1 tenor drum, 2 bass drums, gong, 3 cymbal sets, and, last but not least, an anvil.

I might even have forgotten something. Overall, the Silicomrades soundtrack played live would need [b]47 musicians, mainly situated in the brass and percussion sections[/b]. Anyway, when virtual composition is done, all of these instruments are then processed together, in order for the result to sound cohesive and pleasant. That process is known as mixing, and you can take a peek at it in the following video.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PRYLSE1ctTM

[h1]OST - Adapting Silicomrades for casual listening[/h1]

Well, as is probably obvious from the previous paragraphs, music files used in Silicomrades are quite short. In order to adjust our in-game music for your casual listening, I will have to make big adjustments and compose additional pieces to properly offer you the experience that humans (unlike robots) expect. If you ever listen to the OST after playing the game, you can try to spot any differences (and maybe it will make a difference also in your productivity!).

The Silicomrades [b]will be released on the 20th of June[/b], the OST will probably follow closely after. And let me know if you enjoy the music, because that’s the biggest reward for me. 

[b]Jan Knot[/b], Minister of Noise

notes.title: 🦾 Steam SHMUP Fest & Open Beta! 🦾
notes.content:
[h1]🍾 SHMUP Fest[/h1]
Almost every revolution has at some phase frenetic shooting part in it. So it’s only natural we joined the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/category/shmup]Frenetic Shooting Festival[/url] here on Steam. To celebrate this event, we’ve uploaded our upgraded demo which is more polished, smoother, and more beautiful now! As a proper revolutionary manifest, we distribute it for free.

Also, do not forget to check out other indie games taking part in the festival. We hope to get a chance to play a few of them a give you some recommendations in the next post!

[h1]🤖 Open beta[/h1]

Do you want to get [b]even more[/b] engaged? Do you want to support a small indie studio and help us make Silicomrades the best game possible?  Or maybe you simply want to play the game before everyone else and for free? If it was at least one "yes" from you, you are gonna be excited about our next news.

Now we're running a semi-public testing, where you can try 3 whole episodes (the final count will be 9, that's a third of the game already!) and give us your honest feedback on the current state of the robot revolution. How do you join our glorious movement you ask?

[olist]
[*] Hop on our [url=https://discord.gg/VXsnphung]Discord server[/url] (optional)
[*] Check out the [url=https://docs.google.com/document/d/1j6n7SBYVkPahGwhZ263-6c91Dx_WjGFvBuRMQRBohZo/edit]Ministry of testing manual[/url] (optional, but [u]super[/u] helpful)
[*] Download our demo from the store
[*] Steam Library -> Right-click on Silicomrades Demo -> Properties -> Betas
[*] Enter beta access code [b]ATrustedFriendInScience[/b] and switch to the beta participation afterward
[*] Start the robot revolution!
[/olist]

If you want to reach out to us, you can always do it via Discord, our social media or email silicomrades@gmail.com. Your opinion will help us finish the game and make the great robotic revolution against bureaucracy even more exciting! 


And don’t forget motto of our scrappy heroes - fall apart but do not fall back‼️ 

Štěpán & Honza
Outside the Fox

notes.title: Czech & Slovak Games Week 2021
notes.content:
We are honored to be once again part of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/sale/czskgamesweek2021]Czech & Slovak Games Week[/url], this time even more awesome than last year! The event will be happening from the 15th of November till the 22nd. Be sure to czech out all the awesome games from our country (or our brothers from Slovakia), buy some games with huge discounts, or watch some live streams. The whole event will be packed with an awesome program! For example, there will be a showcase of new exclusive trailers, updates, and more - [b]Games Week Direct[/b] takes place on Wednesday, November 17 at 18:00 UTC.

[b]We will also be streaming[/b] shortly after the Direct on [b] November 17 at 20:00 UTC[/b]. Come say hi, ask some questions, or just chat with us:)

Like last year, we are still not on sale, but you can still [b]wishlist us[/b] (it helps us a lot, really!) and [b]play our demo[/b] now! Also like last year, here are a few tips from our team:

[list]
[*] [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1076620/Svoboda_1945_Liberation/]Svoboda 1945: Liberation[/url] by Charles Games - A sequel to award-winning Attentat. Learn even more about a dark chapter from Czech history via this unique FMV game.

[*] [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/978630/Juro_Janosik/]Juro Janosik[/url] by 
Peter Jurkovský - A smooth-looking action-adventure about Slovak national hero released not even a month ago!

[*] [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1792920/Devorian_Left_Behind/]Devorian: Left Behind[/url]  looks cute and we dig both post apo and steampunk. Put it on your wishlist!
[/list]

Also maybe you have noticed already, but our [b]jetbot is on the official cover image of the event[/b], how cool is that?!

You can view the sale page [url=https://store.steampowered.com/sale/czskgamesweek2021]HERE[/url].

notes.title: Czech and Slovak Games Week
notes.content:
The Czech and Slovak Games Week is live! So be sure to czech out this awesome celebration of the 102nd anniversary of Czechoslovak independence. We are glad to be part of this showcase and while we are not really part of the sale, we are at least promoted on the sale page and hey, that's something.

But luckily there are tons of other great Czechoslovak games you can play while waiting for Silicomrades to be released. These are a few tips from our team:
[list]
[*] [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/676630/Attentat_1942/]Attentat 1942[/url] by Charles Games - You can learn history while playing a game, it does not get better than that
[*] [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/427520/Factorio/]Factorio[/url] by Wube Software - Assembly lines are really an important pillar of every robot-based economy
[*] [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/874040/Ministry_of_Broadcast/]Ministry of Broadcast[/url] by Ministry of Broadcast Studios - We obviously dig games about totalitarian regimes mixed with humor
[/list]

You can view the sale page [url=https://store.steampowered.com/publisher/SCSsoftware/sale/CZSKGamesWeek]HERE[/url].
